text: Outsourcing. They came to us for the outsourcing of payroll and tax.
Payroll. We run payroll for around two hundred companies.
Client portfolio. My client portfolio is mostly services, not industry.
Handle. My team handles the tax side. I handle back office.
Specialise in. We specialise in outsourcing, not in consulting.
Stakeholder. There were ten people on the call. Every one of them was a stakeholder.
Decision-maker. May I ask who the decision-maker is on your side?
Agenda. Shall we agree on an agenda before we start?
Thanks for making the time. I’ve brought David along — I hope that’s all right.
Morning. Sorry, I joined from the car, so forgive the noise.
So. We’re opening a branch in São Paulo in January, and we don’t want to build a finance team from scratch.
What Karen means is that we’d rather outsource the whole thing. Payroll especially. That’s the part that worries me.
David handles operations. I’m on the finance side, so the numbers come to me.
How big is your client portfolio? We’ve been burned by a small firm before.
And do you specialise in foreign companies, or is that occasional?
One more thing — our head office will want to sign off. So this isn’t only us two.
True. Ralph in London is the decision-maker. We just have to convince him.
Right. Shall we go through your agenda, then?
Thanks for making the time.
Before we start, could I ask who's joining us today?
We're a BPO firm. We handle payroll, finance and tax.
May I ask who the decision-maker is on your side?
Let me make sure I understood you correctly.

Hi Fabia, it's Karen Whitfield. Just a quick message before Tuesday. I've invited one person from each area, so there will be five of us on the call. I hope that is not too many. What I would really like to cover first is payroll, because that is where we have had problems with our current provider, and honestly it is the reason we are talking to you at all. The rest can wait. Oh, and could you send a short agenda before the call? With five people, I would rather nobody talked over anybody. Thanks. See you Tuesday.

Right, two minutes before you go in. This one came through the website, and one of our current clients referred them, so they already trust us a little. Use that. There are two names on the invite, but be ready: with these companies more people usually join at the last minute, and nobody introduces themselves. So in the first minute, ask each person to say their name and their area, and write it down. Half of them will be there just to listen. And they will ask about price early. Do not answer that before you know what they actually need. Good luck.
